contexts.label: I smoke or quit within the last year
I take blood thinners (warfarin, DOACs, antiplatelets)

rules.title: May blunt training adaptations
rules.message: High-dose antioxidants taken around training reduced gains in insulin sensitivity, mitochondrial biogenesis, and endurance markers in several trials, because the ROS pulse from exercise is part of the adaptation signal. If you keep them, take them away from workouts or drop the dose. Resveratrol blunted training benefits in older men, and the quercetin data are mixed. See [antioxidant-megadoses-during-training] and [resveratrol-pterostilbene-supplements].

rules.title: Beta-carotene raises lung cancer risk in smokers
rules.message: Beta-carotene supplements increased lung cancer in smokers and asbestos-exposed workers (ATBC, CARET). Check that your formula has no beta-carotene or high-dose vitamin A. See [beta-carotene-supplement].

rules.title: Stacked antioxidants while trying to conceive
rules.message: The best fertility trials of antioxidant combinations (MOXI, FAZST) found no benefit for semen quality, DNA fragmentation, or live birth, and very high antioxidant loads can impair sperm chromatin compaction ('reductive stress'). ESHRE does not recommend antioxidants in IVF. If you use any, one modest-dose product is the evidence-based ceiling. See [high-dose-antioxidant-cocktail] and [male-antioxidant-combination].

rules.title: Iron only with a documented deficiency
rules.message: Iron catalyzes the most damaging oxidant reactions (Fenton chemistry). Supplement it only when ferritin or other tests show deficiency, and re-test. See [iron-excess].

rules.title: Selenium from more than one product
rules.message: Selenium has a narrow U-shaped curve: in people who are already replete, 200 µg/day was linked to higher type 2 diabetes risk. Add up the selenium across all your products and diet (Brazil nuts are very high). See [selenium-supplement].

rules.title: May add to bleeding risk
rules.message: Vitamin E raised hemorrhagic stroke risk in trials, and several polyphenol and curcumin supplements have antiplatelet effects. Tell your prescriber and pharmacist about these.

rules.title: Review every supplement with prenatal care
rules.message: Folic acid (and iodine, per many guidelines) is recommended in pregnancy. Most other supplements lack pregnancy safety data, and some (high-dose vitamin A, many herbal extracts) are best avoided. See [folic-acid].

rules.title: DIM / indole-3-carbinol with tamoxifen
rules.message: DIM lowered levels of tamoxifen's active metabolites in a trial in women taking tamoxifen. Don't combine without your oncologist. See [indole-3-carbinol-dim].

rules.title: Metformin may blunt some training gains
rules.message: In older adults, metformin reduced muscle gains from resistance training (MASTERS) and blunted aerobic fitness and mitochondrial gains; other trials found no blunting. If you take it for diabetes or PCOS, keep taking it, and raise the question with your prescriber. See [metformin].

rules.title: SGLT2 inhibitor + ketogenic diet: ketoacidosis risk
rules.message: SGLT2 inhibitors (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, canagliflozin) combined with very low carbohydrate intake can cause euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis, which is dangerous because blood glucose looks normal. Talk to your prescriber before starting keto. See [sglt2-inhibitors] and [ketogenic-diet].

rules.title: GLP-1 drugs and conception
rules.message: The semaglutide (Wegovy) label advises stopping at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy, and tirzepatide lowers oral contraceptive levels after starting and after each dose increase (use a non-oral or back-up method for 4 weeks). Plan timing with your prescriber. See [glp1-agonists].

rules.title: NSAIDs around ovulation
rules.message: Continuous NSAID use around mid-cycle was linked to luteinized unruptured follicles (the egg isn't released) in a substantial share of cycles in small studies, mostly with COX-2 inhibitors. Occasional use is unlikely to matter; ask about alternatives around ovulation if you use them daily. See [nsaids].

rules.title: Daily NSAIDs and muscle growth
rules.message: Daily high-dose ibuprofen roughly halved quadriceps growth from training in young adults, though not in older adults. See [nsaids].

rules.title: Medications that can affect sperm
rules.message: Some of these affect sperm DNA, counts, hormones, or ejaculation (for example paroxetine raised sperm DNA fragmentation in a small study; 5 mg finasteride and dutasteride lower counts; opioids lower testosterone). Don't stop any prescribed medication on your own; ask the prescriber whether there's a fertility-friendlier option while trying to conceive. Open each item for details.

rules.title: Testosterone shuts down sperm production
rules.message: Exogenous testosterone and anabolic steroids suppress the hormones that drive sperm production, often to zero. Come off only with medical help (often a urologist or reproductive endocrinologist); recovery can take months to over a year. See [testosterone-anabolic-steroids].

rules.title: Antioxidants during chemotherapy or radiation
rules.message: Some trials found worse outcomes with antioxidant supplements during cancer treatment (for example vitamin E during radiotherapy and more second primary cancers), while others found no harm. Clear every supplement with your oncology team. See [antioxidants-during-cancer-treatment].

rules.title: Long-term acid suppressants and nutrients
rules.message: Long-term PPI use is associated with lower B12, iron, and magnesium in observational studies, though a large RCT (COMPASS) found few harms. Worth checking B12 and ferritin if you've used them for years. See [ppi-acid-suppressants].
